title: CAD Engineer Intern
description: Overview Rambus, a premier chip and silicon IP provider making data faster and safer, is seeking to hire an exceptional CAD Engineering Intern to join our Central CAD team in San Jose, California. In this role, you will be working with some of the brightest inventors and engineers in the world developing products that make data faster and safer. As a CAD Engineering Intern, you’ll play a pivotal role in developing automated methodology for chip and silicon IP design. In this role, you’ll report directly to our Director of CAD. Our CAD Team is dedicated to delivering EDA infrastructure, design methodologies, and automation solutions that enable high-performance semiconductor products, including memory interface chips, interconnect solutions, and silicon IP, and your contributions will be instrumental in developing CAD tools, flows, and methodologies for a global design organization. Rambus offers a flexible work environment, embracing a hybrid approach for most office-based roles. Employees are encouraged to spend an average of at least three days per week onsite, allowing for two days of remote work. Responsibilities Develop, maintain, and enhance CAD methodologies and automation flows supporting digital ASIC design, verification and implementation. Work with industry-standard EDA tools across formal verification, synthesis, static timing analysis (STA), power analysis to improve design quality, productivity, and flow efficiency. Develop Python, Tcl, and shell-based scripts and utilities to automate design workflows, analyze results, and streamline engineering processes. Explore and develop AI-assisted solutions to address practical challenges in CAD and semiconductor design workflows, including engineering data analysis, debugging, and workflow Investigate and deploy applications of large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and AI agents for engineering automation and intelligent workflow assistance. Build and integrate AI-enabled utilities with existing engineering tools and workflows, assessing their accuracy, reliability, performance, and practical effectiveness. Collaborate with cross-functional CAD, design, verification, and physical design teams to understand engineering challenges, translate requirements into technical solutions, and validate Gain exposure to broader physical design and signoff methodologies, including place and route (P&R), physical verification (DRC/LVS), and related implementation flows. Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Understanding of digital logic design, RTL, and ASIC/SoC design fundamentals. Familiarity with digital implementation methodology, such as logic synthesis, static timing analysis, or power analysis. Programming or scripting experience in Python, Tcl, Bash, or similar languages. Familiarity with Linux environments and software development fundamentals, including debugging and version control. Strong creative, problem identification, analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills with an ability to work independently and collaborate across teams. Interest in applying automation and emerging AI technologies to engineering problems. Willingness to take lead on work, decisions, actions and consequences. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience with standard EDA tools from Synopsys, Cadence, or Siemens. Understanding of timing constraints, timing closure, power optimization, and PPA tradeoffs. Exposure to place and route (P&R), formal verification, physical verification (DRC/LVS), or related signoff methodologies. Experience with AI/ML technologies, including LLMs, RAG, AI agents, or agentic automation Understand what to build and how to build it, rather than relying entirely on AI tools. Experience developing Python-based tools, MCPs, APIs, or automation frameworks. Up to date knowledge on AI (tools) About Rambus Rambus is a global company that makes industry-leading memory interface chips and Silicon IP to advance data center connectivity and solve the bottleneck between memory and processing. With over 30 years of semiconductor experience, we are a leading provider of high-performance products and innovations that maximize the bandwidth, capacity and security for AI and other data-intensive workloads. Our world-class team is the foundation of our company, and our innovative spirit drives us to develop the cutting-edge products and technologies essential for tomorrow’s systems. Rambus offers a competitive compensation package including base salary, bonus, equity, matching 401(k), employee stock purchase plan, comprehensive medical and dental benefits, time-off program, and gym membership. The US hourly range for this full-time position is $25.80 to $47.80. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location. The successful candidate’s starting pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. At Rambus, we are committed to fostering a workplace where every individual is respected, supported, and empowered to succeed. We value a range of perspectives and experiences that contribute to innovation and collaboration. Our goal is to ensure that all team members have equitable access to opportunities, resources, and a sense of belonging. We believe that a culture of fairness and inclusion helps us all do our best work. Rambus is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. If you require assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please feel free to inform us in your application. title: Virtualisation Software Engineer Intern - Core OS
description: Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas quickly become products, services and experiences that people love. As an intern in the Core Virtualisation team, you'll do real engineering work alongside experienced engineers on technology that ships across the Apple ecosystem. The Core Virtualisation team builds features that bring hardware, system software and apps together into one Apple experience. If you like to know how things work at the lowest level, from CPU architecture to the kernel to the frameworks developers use, this internship is a chance to learn from the people who build them. Description The Virtualisation team builds the core technology that lets developers and users run macOS and other operating systems and environments reliably on their Mac. Our work covers kernel-level support, the Hypervisor framework and the Virtualisation framework. As an intern, you'll own a meaningful project with guidance from a dedicated mentor and support from the wider team. Depending on your interests and the team's needs, you might: - Explore, prototype and build new features in Apple's Hypervisor or Virtualisation frameworks. - Help improve existing features in the Apple virtualisation stacks. - Write tests and test tools that improve the reliability and correctness of virtualisation components. - Investigate and debug issues that span the kernel, the hypervisor, user space and guest operating systems. - Measure and analyse virtual machine performance and look for ways to improve it. - Take part in code reviews and design discussions, and present your work to the team at the end of your internship. You'll write production-quality C and C++, learn how a modern OS and hypervisor work on Apple silicon, and see how hardware and software teams work together to deliver new features. Minimum qualifications Exposure to virtualisation technologies (for example KVM, QEMU, Xen, Hyper-V or similar) through coursework, research, open source or personal projects. Familiarity with the Arm architecture (Armv8/Armv9) or experience with any assembly language. Experience with kernel development, device drivers or bare-metal / embedded programming. Experience debugging low-level software with tools such as LLDB/GDB. Interest in software testing and in designing systems that are easy to test. Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and clear written and verbal communication. Preferred qualifications Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD programme in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical/Electronic Engineering or a related field. Solid programming skills in C and/or C++. Coursework or project experience in at least one of: operating systems, computer architecture, systems programming or compilers. Understanding of core OS concepts such as processes, memory management, and interrupts/exceptions.

title: Mainframe System Verification Tester Apprentice
description: At IBM Infrastructure & Technology, we design and operate the systems that keep the world running. From high-resiliency mainframes and hybrid cloud platforms to networking, automation, and site reliability. Our teams ensure the performance, security, and scalability that clients and industries depend on every day. Working in Infrastructure & Technology means tackling complex challenges with curiosity and collaboration. You'll work with diverse technologies and colleagues worldwide to deliver resilient, future-ready solutions that power innovation. With continuous learning, career growth, and a supportive culture, IBM provides the opportunities to build expertise and shape the infrastructure that drives progress. As a Mainframe System Verification Tester Apprentice at IBM, you will work in IBM Z Engineering System Test and continue the IBM tradition of delivering world-class Z mainframes that are best of breed in Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability. Engineering Systems Test is the final stage of IBM Z server product development where the design, architecture, and code is validated and qualified. You will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and experience using the latest tools and technologies to support IBM processors, storage or other semiconductor hardware. Throughout your apprenticeship, you will work closely with experienced engineers, technicians and other mentors in a laboratory or test floor environment to create and execute test or physical characterization plans that assess the electrical performance and characteristics against design and functional requirements. Where applicable, you will be taught principles of system analysis, defect identification and repair and/or the basics of a variety of lab safety procedures relevant to the physical preparation of samples for chemical, optical, or electrical characterization. To that end, you will be trained in the use of state-of-the-art tools to test, manipulate and inspect product chips, and work with our engineers to interpret and consolidate the obtained data. What is an Apprenticeship? IBM Apprenticeship Program is an official registered apprenticeship recognized by the Department of Labor (DOL). Every graduate of a Registered Apprenticeship program receives a nationally-recognized credential from the DOL. During the apprenticeship duration, you will be required to complete specific learning hours and on the job training that has been outlined to ensure you are developing the skills and competencies essential to the role. You will be able to learn and grow at your own pace, but we expect most apprentices will complete their learning within 12 months. Once you graduate and receive your certificate from our apprentice program, you will be eligible to apply to available full-time roles at IBM. Who you are An apprenticeship is about learning. We’re seeking candidates who have the following requirements, but we know you’re just getting your career started, and we’re committed to helping you learn and grow. If you’ve had some experience with data analysis or simply working in a team oriented environment in the past, you’re exactly the type of candidate we’re looking for. To be successful, you need: Drive and eagerness to learn Ability to work independently, and in an efficient and organized manner Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team Strong troubleshooting Some basic knowledge or experience in electrical engineering sciences i.e. Electrical Safety, Electron Theory, AC/DC Basics, Wires and Cables, Computer Electronics, Electrical Testing Equipment What’s the experience? As an apprentice, you'll join with other apprentices in a local cohort. You'll go through your first few weeks together, learning about IBM and the skills you'll be attaining throughout your apprenticeship. Then, you'll work with your managers and mentors to progress through your personal skills roadmap, learning and demonstrating new knowledge and competencies through hands-on application with your project teams. After completion of initial training (approximately 6 months), you may be required to work an alternate shift (e.g. 2:30-11:00 pm) for a period of approximately 6 months. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Relocation assistance is not available. Willingness to complete the requirements of the apprenticeship program High School Diploma or GED Some knowledge or experience with any of the following: Soldering and de-soldering Electrical Safety Electron Theory AC Basics Computer Electronics Electrical Testing Equipment (i.e multimeters, oscilloscopes, etc) Preferred Technical and Professional Experience - None Required Education - High School Diploma/GED Preferred Education - Associate's Degree/College Diploma United States Infrastructure & Technology Internship POUGHKEEPSIE, US POUGHKEEPSIE (0147) International Business Machines Corporation Education Electrical Safety Electronics Multimeters Soldering Electrical Testing Professionalism

title: Research Scientist Intern - Audio Systems
description: Meta's Hardware Audio Team is hiring a PhD Research Scientist Intern to help push the audio performance of next-generation wearables, where small speakers have to deliver full, rich sound. This internship focuses on finding ways to unlock the full capability of every speaker to deliver the highest possible audio quality. It spans our audio hardware and audio experience teams, and the work runs from measurement and analysis through prototyping and validating new methods on real devices. The project is intentionally open-ended: working with the engineers and researchers, you will help identify the most impactful directions. The ideal candidate has a strong research background in electroacoustics, loudspeaker modeling, acoustic measurement and digital signal processing (DSP). Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long, and we have various start dates throughout the year.

title: Performance Engineering Intern - Platform Performance and Power
location: Canada; Santa Clara, CA; United States
description: NVIDIA’s Performance Lab is hiring a Platform Performance and Power Intern responsible for completing post-silicon performance and power benchmarking on NVIDIA and competitive GPU products. This work covers notebook, desktop, workstation, and embedded platforms using industry-standard tools and applications. Compiled and analyzed data is provided to internal software, hardware, sales, and marketing groups to inform decisions. The position also requires Python scripting to automate testing and develop tools that improve workflow. Preferred duration of the internship: 8 months minimum What you’ll be doing Implement hands-on tests focusing on performance and power on current GPU platforms across real world applications from gaming, professional visualization, and AI. Set up and maintain test systems by configuring hardware, operating systems, drivers, and software tools used for benchmarking and data collection. Analyze benchmark and power data, turning raw results into clear reports that help hardware, software, and product teams improve GPU efficiency and performance. Debug issues that arise during testing—whether related to applications, scripts, or hardware—and work with other engineering teams to resolve them. Contribute data and insights that influence future GPU builds and help compare NVIDIA products against competing solutions. Develop, implement, and maintain automation tools to improve testing efficiency. What we need to see: Pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Hands-on programming experience with Python, including writing scripts for automation, data processing, or testing. Academic or project experience with computer architecture fundamentals Experience with lab equipment such as DMMs, Agilent DAQs, or National Instruments DAQs. Exposure to performance or power measurement, including collecting, comparing, and interpreting results from experiments or coursework. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Interested in GPU technology and how hardware and software work together to improve performance per watt. Familiarity with electrical fundamentals or lab equipment used for power measurement, such as multimeters or data acquisition tools. Experience with running application-based benchmarks across Gaming, ProViz, AI domains. Passionate about learning, collaborating with engineers from different fields, and contributing to real product decisions. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us and our best-in-class engineering teams are rapidly growing. We are building a team that will help shape the future of data center computing. If you are passionate about new technologies, care about improving efficiency and quality, and want to be at the forefront of technology, we would love for you to join us. Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rate for this position is 20 USD – 71 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 14, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. The Networks Operations TAC SME team supports the operational reliability and performance of Samsung’s 4G and 5G wireless network solutions. The team collaborates with all operational support levels including the customer facing Technical Assistance Center (TAC), Engineering, R&D, and other customer-facing organizations to investigate complex network issues, identify recurring failure patterns, improve troubleshooting processes, and reduce service-restoration time. The intern will also evaluate related technical content—including product documentation, MOPs, troubleshooting guides, knowledge articles, alarms, and system logs - recommend efficient troubleshooting steps and surface relevant technical guidance based on reported symptoms and network context. Coursework or project experience in one or more areas such as machine learning, predictive analytics, natural-language processing, generative AI, or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
